title: Make study fetch firstmate at a pinned SHA, readable by its agents
summary: Study is already registered in the CLI wiring, so the remaining work is fetching firstmate at a pinned SHA. Add a core hook that runs at study job start, pins the source, and puts the tree inside the agents' confined, read-only working area. Cover the dispatch call with a test, and fix the retry's two findings: the unreadable source and the missing hook test.

defaults_applied.how: Recovered the pin location, the earlier blocker and the hook design from the repository and the rejection findings instead of asking for them.
A dispatch test enforces the hook call. The pin check errors on any SHA mismatch.
New tests for the hook at dispatch, the pin, and agent read access. Clippy and fmt stay clean.
One focused change: the hook, the pin, and its config.
Use the existing athena-git wrapper and system git to fetch. No new fetch crate.
Only a public repository URL and a SHA go into config.

assumptions: Wiring already registers Study (crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs:22), so the reader's catalog should list it. The job only verifies that and does not rebuild it.
No pinned firstmate SHA is in the repository, so the SHA and URL go in athena.toml under [capabilities.study]. The producer must not invent a SHA, and the config value is the single source of truth.
Fetching runs in Athena's own process (git clone or fetch plus checkout of the exact SHA). Agents keep no network access.

The pinned tree is exposed to the producer and verifier inside their snapshot directory as a read-only path that is excluded from the candidate change list. This fixes the earlier blocker: the source sat at <job_dir>/source, outside the policy root.
The fetch is skipped or fails clearly when the pin is missing or the clone is unreachable. Tests use a local git repository as the source and never touch the network.
The study capability's cargo grants use offline mode (CARGO_NET_OFFLINE or --offline) if cargo is granted at all.
question: What is the firstmate commit SHA to pin (the repository is https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate)? If you don't answer, the producer takes the SHA from a config value you supply later, and the job cannot choose one itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena_core::capability::Capability gains a default no-op job-start hook that returns a brief note and extra env. Study overrides it to pin its configured source. Change keeps the default behavior.
run.rs calls the hook at job start, before the producer runs. The note appears in the producer and verifier briefs, and the env reaches the agents.

The pinned source tree is materialized inside each agent's confined working directory (producer snapshot and verifier snapshot), read-only, and excluded from the candidate change list and admission. The path the brief names resolves inside the policy root.
athena.toml gains a [capabilities.study] section with the firstmate URL and a full 40-hex pinned SHA, plus grants, and it is named in this criterion. Study cargo grants run offline.
The study fetch verifies that the checked-out HEAD equals the pinned SHA and errors otherwise. A malformed or missing pin gives a clear error.

Run `cargo test`. A dispatch-level test with a fake capability (in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs or athena-core tests) shows the hook ran, its note reached the brief and its env reached the agents. It fails if the run.rs call is removed.

Run `cargo test`. A study test builds a local git repository, pins its SHA, and shows the tree is readable through the agent path policy (Read, Grep and Glob accepted) and absent from the change list.
Run `cargo test` and the reader catalog test. The catalog rendered for the reader lists both change and study, and the reader schema's capability enum includes study.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All pass.

out_of_scope: Studying firstmate, or any claim about what firstmate does.
Running firstmate, containment, replay, or publishing.
Hermes Agent or Athena itself as study sources.
Changes to the change capability's behavior.
departures: Larger than the reference: it touches the core, the agent path policy, and config, and the previous attempt was rejected on a blocker. Cost, time and the verification pass rate are all set worse than the reference.
